commit.message:
Refresh the out of date app warning instead of only at launch (#675) (#679)

`AppState.buildBehind` was read once at launch, and its own note said the answer
could not change while the app was open. It can: the running app is compared
against the newest commit in the code folder, and the code folder moves while
PostRoll sits there. A session that pulls, or switches to a branch ahead of the
build, left the running copy out of date with nothing saying so, which is the
state that makes a shipped fix look like it never worked.

The same treatment #668 gave the checkout notice. Every reading of the folder
now carries the folder with it, so the verdict is taken again off the reading
that already goes out rather than by adding a second reader, which includes the
one every generation takes for its own log.

What is new here is the dismissal. The notice is a banner and can simply
reappear; this is a sheet in the middle of the window, so a verdict Dan has
waved away is remembered and not put back. Identity is the pair of times, so
work merging afterwards is a different verdict and says so, catching up clears
the memory outright, and a verdict that could not be reached leaves whatever is
showing alone rather than reporting a currency nobody measured.
